children: is pursuing an investment-grade bond sale to raise approximately $4B to refinance debt as the company's revenue continues to surge due to AI-driven demand for its servers, according to Bloomberg.

The company is offering bonds in multiple tranches with maturities ranging from three to 10 years, according to people familiar with the issue, the report said. Funds raised will be used to pay off outstanding notes due this year and to provide for general corporate purposes. The financial firms handling the bond offering include Barclays
"Dell has room to refinance maturities and increase shareholder returns while preserving its mid-BBB credit profile," said Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Robert Schiffman, according to the report.

Dell's shares have more than quadrupled year to date as its revenue has surged on the back of AI-driven server demand. Last week, Dell boosted its AI server revenue guidance for fiscal 2027 to $74B, up from $60B previously.
Shares moved up another 3.5% during Wednesday's market action.

title: Dell pursues $4B from bond sale to refinance debt: report
